title: Body Burden of Dichlorodiphenyl Dichloroethene (DDE) and Childhood Pulmonary Function.
ehr_evidence: Data came from an environmental epidemiologic cohort study conducted in central Germany (South-Hesse, 1994-1997) with prospectively collected blood DDE measurements (high-resolution gas chromatography), pulmonary function tests, and self-administered questionnaires; no electronic health record was used.
summary: In a longitudinal cohort of children aged 8-10 years in central Germany (1994-1997), higher blood DDE levels were associated with lower FVC and FEV1 at 10 years, mediated through reduced height and weight.
key_findings: Linear mixed models showed no significant direct associations between blood DDE and pulmonary function: FVC estimate 0.006 (SE 0.02, p=0.71), FEV1 estimate 0.004 (SE 0.02, p=0.81), FEV1/FVC estimate 0.12 (SE 0.43, p=0.78).

Path analysis showed DDE measured at 8 years had significant, inverse, indirect, and total effects on FVC at 10 years (-0.18 L per µg/L of DDE, n=328) and FEV1 (-0.17 L per µg/L of DDE, n=328), mediated through effects on height and weight.
DDE had direct inverse effects on height (total -0.28 cm per µg/L) and weight (total -0.24 kg per µg/L) but no direct effect on FVC or FEV1.
No direct or indirect effects of DDE on FEV1/FVC were found.
Stratified path analyses showed significant indirect negative effects of DDE on FVC (-0.25 L/µg/L in females, -0.21 L/µg/L in males) and FEV1 (-0.24 L/µg/L in females, -0.19 L/µg/L in males).
captured_features: Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1)
study_design: Longitudinal cohort study with linear mixed models for repeated measurements and structural equation (path) analysis
population: Children aged 8-10 years in South-Hesse, central Germany, recruited 1994-1997; 691 participated and 328-344 had both DDE and pulmonary function data
exposure_domain: Organochlorine pesticide (DDE, a DDT metabolite) / persistent organic pollutant
limitations: DDE exposure was not measured at age 9 years and values were carried forward from age 8 years.
Stratified analyses by sex had reduced statistical power due to smaller sample sizes (153 girls, 191 boys).
Single historical cohort from a region without ongoing high DDT application, limiting generalizability.
